summary_hint: Master policy <policy_number> from <insurance_carrier> for <condominium_project_name> (assoc. <association_or_named_insured>), <effective_date>–<expiration_date>: <blanket/scheduled>, RCV <yes/no>, unit scope <walls-in/bare-walls>, GL <limit>, fidelity <amount/none> — the adequacy inputs CO-3 checks, incl. the fidelity coverage the example fires on.

typed_core.name: association_or_named_insured
typed_core.why: CO-3 — the HOA named insured on the master policy

typed_core.name: condominium_project_name
typed_core.why: CO-3 — must match the subject project; identity

typed_core.name: policy_number
typed_core.why: PII (restricted) — policy identity; promote so it is masked, not left unmasked in the catch-all

typed_core.name: policy_form_and_coverage_basis
typed_core.why: CO-3 disambiguator — the form (e.g. special-form / all-risk) sets what 'adequate' means

typed_core.name: effective_date
typed_core.why: CO-3 — the master policy must be in force through closing

typed_core.name: expiration_date
typed_core.why: CO-3 — must remain valid through closing

typed_core.name: blanket_or_scheduled_coverage
typed_core.why: CO-3 — blanket vs scheduled changes how building limits satisfy adequacy

typed_core.name: replacement_cost_indicator
typed_core.why: CO-3 disambiguator — RCV vs ACV; the settlement-basis lesson — the same 'replacement cost' wording can attach to a different coverage row
typed_core.prompt_hint: Read the RCV/ACV basis from the building coverage row, not the first 'replacement cost' on the page

typed_core.name: coinsurance_percentage
typed_core.why: CO-3 — a coinsurance clause can render limits inadequate (a penalty on underinsurance)

typed_core.name: walls_in_bare_walls_or_single_entity_scope
typed_core.why: CO-3 — walls-in vs bare-walls vs single-entity determines whether unit interiors are covered by the master or need HO-6

typed_core.name: water_damage_or_master_policy_exclusions
typed_core.why: CO-3 — material exclusions are the 'inadequacy' CO-3 flags

typed_core.name: fidelity_crime_coverage_present
typed_core.why: CO-3 — the example: 'no fidelity coverage where required → fire'
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture presence explicitly — absence where required is the CO-3 fire

typed_core.name: fidelity_crime_coverage_amount
typed_core.why: CO-3 — the fidelity/crime limit checked against the requirement

typed_core.name: flood_coverage_present
typed_core.why: processor/CO-3 — whether the master carries flood (warrantability where the project is in an SFHA)

typed_core.name: agent_contact_and_certificate_date
typed_core.why: recency/processor — who issued the evidence and when (COI date); follow-up

nested_lists.name: building_limits
nested_lists.shape_reason: a project has 1–several insured buildings, each with a limit and (often) its own deductible — few-to-moderate items, so a flat row is light

fields.name: wind_hail_named_storm_deductible
fields.why: CO-3 — separate wind/hail/named-storm deductible (often a percentage, so degrade to str)

fields.name: source
fields.why: provenance — the row the value came from

rejected.name: document_title, form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: classification/version before extraction (policy_form_and_coverage_basis identifies the form)

rejected.name: issuer_address, issuer_phone, issuer_email_or_url
rejected.reason: carrier contact; captured via agent_contact where relevant; catch-all

rejected.name: document_issue_date
rejected.reason: duplicates the certificate date in agent_contact_and_certificate_date

rejected.name: statement_period_start/_end
rejected.reason: the policy term is effective/expiration, not a statement period

rejected.name: party_names, party_addresses
rejected.reason: the association is captured; no individual parties on a master policy

rejected.name: property_address
rejected.reason: covered by condominium_project_name + the building rows

rejected.name: loan_number
rejected.reason: not on a master policy (a unit's mortgagee clause lives on the unit's evidence)

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block
rejected.reason: a policy/COI is issued by the carrier, not executed/notarized

rejected.name: covered_property_addresses_or_buildings
rejected.reason: merged into the building_limits per-building rows

rejected.name: property_deductibles, wind_hail_named_storm_deductibles
rejected.reason: merged into the building_limits rows as deductible columns

rejected.name: ordinance_law_and_equipment_breakdown, boiler_machinery_or_equipment_breakdown
rejected.reason: secondary coverages; no CO-3 adequacy gate; catch-all

rejected.name: mortgagee_or_certificate_holder
rejected.reason: on a master policy the mortgagee clause is per-unit on the unit's evidence, not the master; catch-all unless a rule needs it

encoding_variations: replacement_cost_indicator — 'Replacement Cost', 'RCV', 'Guaranteed Replacement Cost', 'ACV'. No boolean coercer; the basis may attach to the building coverage vs another row — read the building-coverage row (the settlement-basis lesson)
blanket_or_scheduled_coverage — 'Blanket', 'Scheduled', 'Blanket by building'; blanket limits cover all buildings collectively

walls_in_bare_walls_or_single_entity_scope — 'Walls-in / all-in', 'Bare-walls / studs-out', 'Single-entity', 'Original specifications'. No enum coercer; determines whether a separate HO-6 walls-in policy is needed

fidelity/crime — labeled 'Fidelity Bond', 'Employee Dishonesty', 'Crime Coverage', 'Commercial Crime'. Present-vs-absent and the limit are the two facts CO-3 needs; a $0/absent bond where required is the fire
general liability — '$1,000,000 each occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate'; capture the each-occurrence limit as the adequacy input
coinsurance — '80%', '90%', 'Agreed Value (no coinsurance)'. No percent coercer; degrade to str; 'agreed value' waives the penalty

open_questions.q: BLOCKED status — CO-3 has no producer yet. Confirm the schema should land the adequacy fields now so the rule lights up when unblocked
options: wait until CO-3 has a producer

open_questions.q: Merging three object[] into one building_limits list — the catalog separates building limits, property deductibles, and wind/hail deductibles
options: one per-building row carrying limit + deductibles (chosen, honors the one-nested-list budget)
separate lists if buildings and deductibles do not align 1:1
open_questions.recommendation: (a) one per-building row; flag (b) if a real blanket policy does not map cleanly per building GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: Fidelity flattening — fidelity_or_crime_coverage (object) is flattened to present-flag + amount. Confirm those two are the CO-3 inputs
open_questions.recommendation: the schema lands the coverage fact and leaves the requirement math (e.g. 3 months of assessments) to CO-3

open_questions.q: RCV basis disambiguation — replacement_cost_indicator must reflect the building coverage (the settlement-basis lesson)
options: prompt the model to read the building row
open_questions.recommendation: prompt the model to read the building row; flag if misreads appear

notes: The catalog splits building_limits, property_deductibles, and wind_hail_named_storm_deductibles into three object[] structures and adds covered_property_addresses_or_buildings. Per the one-nested-list budget, these are merged into a single per-building row (limit + deductibles + identity).
No borrower PII: a master condo policy names the association, not individual owners; association_or_named_insured and insurance_carrier are entities.
Ambiguity: flood_coverage_present is tagged 'processor/CO-3' — classed processor as primary but it also serves CO-3 (warrantability); flagged.
